einzeiler: How the events of 9/11 reshaped U.S. national security and intelligence
kurzfassung: Host Mary Louise Kelly and former top intelligence officials discuss what happened behind closed doors on September 11. They examine the new national security architecture built to confront these threats and whether it has worked. The conversation also explores how the events of that day continue to shape global affairs.
stichpunkte: Discussion on what happened behind closed doors on 9/11
Evaluation of the new national security architecture built after the attacks
Assessment of whether the U.S. is safer today
Analysis of how 9/11 continues to shape global events
Insights from former top officials Stephen Hadley, Jane Harman, John McLaughlin, and Michael Morell
beschreibung:
September 11th presented a new kind of national security threat, so a new national security architecture was built to confront it. Has it worked? Are we safer?

This special episode from Sources & Methods, the national security podcast from NPR, host Mary Louise Kelly and former top intelligence officials discuss what happened behind closed doors on 9/11, and how the events of that day are still shaping global events.

Those officials were Stephen Hadley, Jane Harman, John Mclaughlin and Michael Morell. At the time of the attacks, Hadley was serving as deputy national security adviser in the Bush White House. Harman was a Democratic member of Congress representing California. McLaughlin was deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency. Morell was also at the CIA and was President Bush's CIA briefer that very day.

This episode was recorded in front of a studio audience at NPR headquarters in Washington D.C. on September 9.
